assistant.template.agentNoName.text: Agent {n} has no name (or one over 60 characters).
assistant.template.agentNoName.note: Why a template file can't be used: its agent number {n} (1, 2…) has no usable name.

assistant.template.badMcp.text: {name}'s MCP servers aren't a list Hive can use.
assistant.template.badMcp.note: Why a template file can't be used: an agent's list of MCP servers.

assistant.template.badName.text: Its name is missing or longer than {max} characters.
assistant.template.badName.note: Why a template file can't be used: the template's name.

assistant.template.badPairs.text: Its pairs of builders and reviewers name agents it doesn’t have, or an agent twice.
assistant.template.badPairs.note: Why a template file can't be used: its list of builders paired with reviewers (glossary: builder, reviewer) doesn't match its agents.

assistant.template.badRole.text: {name}'s role in the workflow isn't builder, reviewer, either or generalist.
assistant.template.badRole.note: Why a template file can't be used: an agent's role in the workflow (glossary: builder, reviewer, either) is none of the three. Keep builder, reviewer and either as they are (the file's values).

assistant.template.badToken.text: {name} uses {token}: an agent’s name may only hold '{key}' (the project’s key) and '{n}' (its number among the agents with that name).
assistant.template.badToken.note: Why a template file can't be used: an agent's name pattern ({name}) holds {token}, a token Hive doesn't know. The quoted '{key}' and '{n}' are shown as {key} and {n}: keep them, with their straight quotes, as they are.

assistant.template.from09.text: This template is from Hive 0.9 and can't be loaded in 1.0. Recreate it from your agents with Save as Template.
assistant.template.from09.note: Why a template file can't be used: Hive 0.9 made it (its agents had worktrees of their own; 1.0's don't). Save as Template is a command: as Hive names it.

assistant.template.longNote.text: The note of agent {name} is over {max, number} characters.
assistant.template.longNote.note: Why a template file can't be used: an agent's note (what it is for, in the user's words) is too long. {max} is the limit, a number. A noun before the name (glossary §1 rule 4).

assistant.template.newer.text: It was made by a newer version of Hive: update Hive to use it.
assistant.template.newer.note: Why a template file can't be used: a newer Hive made it.

assistant.template.noAgents.note: Why a template file can't be used: it holds no agents.

assistant.template.noVersion.text: It isn't a Hive agent template (no version).
assistant.template.noVersion.note: Why a template file can't be used: it has no format version.

assistant.template.notTemplate.text: It isn't a Hive agent template.
assistant.template.notTemplate.note: Why a template file can't be used: it isn't one.

assistant.template.sameName.note: Why a template file can't be used: two agents share a name.

assistant.template.tooMany.text: It has {count} agents; a project can have up to {max}.
assistant.template.tooMany.note: Why a template file can't be used: more agents than any project can have.
